quiz.title: T4.5: Uses Post-Conditionals and Control Flow
quiz.description: Scenario-based questions on post-conditionals (command:condition), QUIT vs RETURN, Boolean evaluation rules (any nonzero/nonempty = true), for/while loops, $SELECT, and CONTINUE in ObjectScript.

questions.question:
While reviewing code you notice the following statement:

set:$GET(person)="" phone = "Unknown"

Which of the following best describes what this line does?
options: The assignment executes only when person is undefined or holds an empty string; in that case phone is set to "Unknown". Otherwise the line is skipped.
The line always sets both person and phone to "Unknown" in a single statement, regardless of their previous values.
Because $GET(person) returns "" only when person is undefined, this line always raises an error before phone can be assigned.
The statement checks whether phone already equals "Unknown"; if so, it clears the variable person by setting it to the empty string.
questions.explanation: The post-conditional Set:condition executes the SET command only when the condition is true. $GET(person) returns "" if person is undefined OR if it explicitly holds "". So $GET(person)="" is true in both cases, and phone gets set to "Unknown". If person has any non-empty value, the entire SET is skipped. (Reference: InterSystems Practice Q18; https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_commands#GCOS_commands_postconditional)

questions.question: A developer is confused about Boolean evaluation. Which of the following values is considered TRUE (non-zero) in an ObjectScript Boolean context?
questions.explanation: ObjectScript evaluates Boolean values by converting to numeric. Empty string converts to 0 (false). 0 is false. "abc" has no leading numeric portion and converts to 0 (false). "1abc" starts with 1, so it converts to 1 (true). Any non-zero numeric value is considered true. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators#GCOS_operators_boolean)

questions.question: You are auditing code for Boolean logic bugs. Which of the following ObjectScript values evaluate to FALSE (0)? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: All are false except 1. Empty string, 0, "0", and "0.0" are all numerically zero. "abc" has no leading digits, so it converts to 0 (false). Only non-zero numeric values (like 1, -5, 3.14, "2dogs") are true. This is a critical concept for post-conditionals. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators#GCOS_operators_boolean)

questions.question:
You are categorizing values using post-conditionals. Consider:

set x = 10
set:x>5 result = "big"
set:x<5 result = "small"
write result

What is the output?
questions.explanation: x=10. The first post-conditional x>5 is true, so result is set to "big". The second post-conditional x<5 is false (10 is not less than 5), so that SET is skipped. Write outputs "big". (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_commands#GCOS_commands_postconditional)

RETURN exits the entire method immediately, regardless of how many nested loops or blocks surround it. When i=2, RETURN "found" exits the method and returns "found". If QUIT were used instead, it would only exit the for loop, and execution would continue to RETURN "not found". (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_creturn)

questions.question:
You are tracing the execution of a loop with a post-conditional quit. Consider:

for i = 1:1:5 {
  quit:i=3
  write i, " "
}
write "done"

What is the output?
questions.explanation: The loop writes 1 (i=1), then writes 2 (i=2). When i=3, the post-conditional Quit:i=3 is true, so QUIT exits the For loop before the Write. Execution continues after the loop with Write "done". Output: "1 2 done". (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_cquit)

questions.question:
You are using post-conditionals with the Write command. Consider:

set status = "active"
write:status="active" "Online"
write:status="inactive" "Offline"

What is the output?
questions.explanation: Post-conditionals work with Write and most other commands. Write:status="active" executes because the condition is true. Write:status="inactive" is skipped because the condition is false. Only "Online" is output. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_commands#GCOS_commands_postconditional)

questions.question: Which ObjectScript commands support post-conditionals (command:condition)? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Most ObjectScript commands support post-conditionals: SET, DO, QUIT, WRITE, KILL, NEW, CONTINUE, and many others. However, FOR and IF do NOT support post-conditionals because they already have their own conditional logic built in. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_commands#GCOS_commands_postconditional)

questions.question:
You are counting odd numbers using Continue with a post-conditional. Consider:

set count = 0
for i = 1:1:10 {
  continue:i#2=0
  set count = count + 1
}
write count

What is the output?
questions.explanation: Continue:i#2=0 skips the rest of the loop body when i is even (i modulo 2 equals 0). So count is incremented only for odd values of i: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 = 5 times. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_ccontinue)

ObjectScript converts "3.5abc" to numeric by extracting the leading numeric portion: 3.5. Since 3.5 is non-zero, the Boolean evaluation is true. This is consistent with the weak typing rules used everywhere in ObjectScript. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators#GCOS_operators_boolean)

questions.question:
You are testing whether a Do post-conditional skips execution. Consider:

set x = ""
do:x ..MyMethod()
write "End"

ClassMethod MyMethod()
{
  write "Called "
}

What is the output?
questions.explanation: Do:x evaluates x as a Boolean condition. Since x="" which converts to 0 (false), the DO is not executed and MyMethod is never called. Only "End" is written. An empty string is always false in ObjectScript. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_commands#GCOS_commands_postconditional)

questions.question:
You are using $SELECT for a compact conditional. Consider:

set x = "cat"
write $SELECT(x="dog":"Woof", x="cat":"Meow", 1:"Unknown")

What is the output?
questions.explanation: $SELECT evaluates conditions left to right and returns the value associated with the first true condition. x="dog" is false, x="cat" is true, so it returns "Meow". The 1:"Unknown" acts as a default case (1 is always true). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fselect)

questions.question:
A developer forgot the default case in $SELECT. Consider:

write $SELECT(0:"A", 0:"B")

What happens?
questions.explanation: If no condition in $SELECT evaluates to true, ObjectScript throws a <SELECT> error. Always include a default case using 1:defaultValue as the last condition to prevent this error. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_fselect)

questions.question: Which of the following values evaluate to TRUE in an ObjectScript Boolean context? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: In ObjectScript, a value is TRUE if its numeric interpretation is nonzero. 1 is true. -5 is true (nonzero). "2dogs" interprets as 2 (true). " 3" with a leading space interprets as 0 (false) because ObjectScript's numeric conversion stops at the first non-numeric character, and a leading space is non-numeric in this context. "00" converts to 0 (false). ".5test" converts to 0.5 (true, nonzero). (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=GCOS_operators)

QUIT with an argument (QUIT i) is not allowed inside a FOR block -- it produces a <COMMAND> error. Inside a FOR loop, QUIT (without an argument) exits the loop, while QUIT expr is only valid for exiting a method with a return value. To return from the method, use RETURN i instead of QUIT i. (Reference: https://docs.intersystems.com/irislatest/csp/docbook/DocBook.UI.Page.cls?KEY=RCOS_cquit)
